name: OVHcloud

profile.reading:
OVHcloud Hillsboro is one of two data centers that anchored OVHcloud's entry into the United States market, located at 1300 Northeast 25th Avenue in Hillsboro, Oregon, inside the Portland area technology corridor often called the Silicon Forest that also hosts major semiconductor and networking operations. OVHcloud is a French cloud and hosting company, one of Europe's largest, that builds and operates the great majority of its own data centers and designs much of its own server hardware rather than buying capacity from third party colocation providers. The Hillsboro facility opened in 2018, alongside a sister site in Vint Hill, Virginia that gave OVHcloud its first US East and US West presence, and the company marked both sites' fifth anniversary with a public announcement in 2023.

OVHcloud has publicly described the technology inside its US data centers, including this one, as built around a proprietary water cooling system rather than conventional air conditioning. The company states this approach helps it achieve some of the lowest power usage effectiveness ratings in the industry, since moving heat with water is markedly more efficient than cooling a data hall with chilled air. OVHcloud also promotes a vertically integrated model in which it designs, builds, operates and eventually recycles its own servers, extending hardware through a second or third operational life before disposal, a sustainability posture the company ties directly to facilities like Hillsboro.

Beyond that, OVHcloud has not published a power capacity figure in megawatts, a square footage or white space figure, or formal certifications specific to the Hillsboro building, and this entry does not estimate those numbers. As of the company's most recent public infrastructure count, Hillsboro sits among roughly three dozen OVHcloud data centers worldwide, spanning Europe, North America and Asia Pacific, used to host the company's public cloud, private cloud, dedicated server and web hosting product lines for customers across the Americas. Given OVHcloud's ownership model, capacity at this site is presumed to serve OVHcloud's own multi tenant customer base directly rather than a single anchor tenant, though the company does not publish a tenant list for any individual facility. No county permit or expansion filing specific to this address has been reviewed for this entry.

profile.reading:
OVH US East Vint Hill is one of two data centers that marked OVHcloud's entry into the United States, located on Watson Court within the Vint Hill Farms area of Fauquier County, Virginia, roughly 40 miles southwest of Washington, DC. OVHcloud is a French cloud and hosting company, one of the largest in Europe, that generally builds and operates its own data centers and designs much of its own server hardware rather than leasing capacity as a colocation tenant. This site opened in 2018 alongside a sister facility in Hillsboro, Oregon, giving OVHcloud parallel East Coast and West Coast anchors in the American market, and the company publicly marked both sites' fifth anniversary in 2023.

The Vint Hill area itself has a long institutional history as a government communications and training site before its later redevelopment into a mixed use business and technology park, which today hosts data centers, light industrial tenants and office users drawn by existing power infrastructure and a location outside the densest and most competitive parts of the Northern Virginia data center market in Loudoun County. That context helps explain why a European cloud provider would choose Fauquier County over the more crowded Ashburn corridor for a facility built to serve its own network rather than to attract third party colocation tenants.

OVHcloud has described the technology inside this facility, as with its other data centers, as built around a proprietary water cooling system that the company says helps deliver some of the lowest power usage effectiveness ratings in the industry, along with a vertically integrated approach to designing, building and eventually recycling its own servers across multiple operational lifecycles. Beyond those general statements, OVHcloud has not published a power capacity figure, square footage, or formal certifications specific to this Vint Hill building, and no such figures are estimated here. Given OVHcloud's ownership and operating model, this site most likely supports the company's own public cloud, private cloud and dedicated server products for customers across the Americas rather than a single outside anchor tenant, though OVHcloud does not publish a per site tenant list. No county permit or zoning record specific to this address has been reviewed for this entry.

reading:
OVHcloud is a French cloud provider headquartered in Roubaix, founded in November 1999 by Octave Klaba with family members Henry, Haline and Miroslaw Klaba, and listed on Euronext Paris under the ticker OVH since October 2021, joining the SBF120 index that December. It appears in this registry as a colocation operator, but that is a loose fit. OVHcloud is a vertically integrated cloud company that designs and assembles its own servers, builds and runs its own buildings, and uses its own direct liquid cooling rather than buying wholesale space from someone else. Its public argument for that integration is cost and lifecycle, and it says it gives servers a second or third life before recycling them.

The company entered the United States around 2018 with two sites, Hillsboro in Oregon and Vint Hill in Virginia, and marked five years of US operation in May 2023, at which point it described those two buildings as two of 34 data centres worldwide and about 200 US staff across two offices. The registry's Oregon row is the Hillsboro site. OVHcloud publishes no capacity figure for Hillsboro, no square footage, no utility service rating and no critical IT load, and the registry records none. Any megawatt number circulating for the Hillsboro building comes from third party trackers rather than from OVHcloud, and should not be read as either IT load or utility service.

The substantive public record for this site is the City of Hillsboro's, not the operator's, and Hillsboro publishes an unusual amount. As of July 2026 the city counted 23 data centre sites, 16 built on about 346 acres and seven in permitting or under construction on about 224 acres, roughly 570 acres out of the city's 17,378. It reports that data centres used about 111 million gallons of water in 2025 across roughly 14 sites, around 1.76 per cent of total city water demand. On tax, the city runs an enterprise zone giving a full property tax exemption on new investment for three to five years. It counted 50 active agreements as of March 2025, 33 of them data centre related, with 17 further data centre applications arriving by March 2026. In 2025 twelve data centre entities held about 7.2 billion dollars of exempted value while data centres still paid about 61.1 million dollars in taxes. Power comes from Portland General Electric, and Oregon's 2025 POWER Act, House Bill 3546, moved the cost of grid additions onto large users.

Two limits on that record matter here. Oregon law lets the city redact company names from published enterprise zone agreements, so none of the city's figures can be attributed to OVHcloud in particular, and this entry does not attribute them. And the record has turned adversarial. Hillsboro and Washington County were sued in June 2026 over data centre tax breaks, the city council directed staff on 9 June 2026 to examine code amendments, enterprise zone changes and environmental impact studies, and on 27 July 2026 the council imposed a 120 day moratorium on new data centre and battery storage land use applications. The moratorium reaches new applications rather than facilities already operating, so it does not by itself change anything about the OVHcloud building already in the ground.
